history.period: Origin claimed 15th century A.D. (UNVERIFIED — exact dates unclear)
history.summary: Hilltop Shiva temple atop Ranchi Hill (Richi Buru, also Tiriburu), at 2,140 ft above sea level and ~350 ft above ground, reached by 468 steps; some sources date it to the 15th century A.D., but this is UNVERIFIED. The hill was known as Phansi Tongri ('hanging hill') in the British era, where freedom fighters were reportedly hanged; the national flag is unfurled here on Independence and Republic Days. The main shrine houses a swayambhu Shivlinga (locally called Pahari Baba), and the campus holds sub-shrines to Mahakaal, Kali, Vishwanath, Hanuman, Durga and Naag. The Shravan Mela draws huge crowds. Major renovation of pathways and lighting was done around 2010. Geocoded exactly to Pahari Mandir, Ratu Road, Ranchi (23.38468, 85.28762).

name: Pahari Mandir, Ranchi
town_description: Ranchi is the capital city of Jharkhand, set on the Chota Nagpur plateau at around 650 m elevation. Known for its waterfalls, lakes and tribal culture, it was the summer capital of undivided Bihar. The city is a commercial and educational hub of the state with rail and air links to major Indian cities.

travel.road: City-centre location off Ratu Road; reach by local bus/auto, then climb 468 steps (verify)
